title.value: Smart About Meds (SAM): a pilot randomized controlled trial of a mobile application to improve medication adherence following hospital discharge
title.justification: The title explicitly mentions the primary focus of the research: evaluating a mobile application called 'Smart About Meds' (SAM) to improve medication adherence.
title.quote: Smart About Meds (SAM): a pilot randomized controlled trial of a mobile application to improve medication adherence following hospital discharge

analysis.description: The paper discusses a pilot randomized controlled trial of a mobile application called Smart About Meds (SAM), designed to improve medication adherence among patients discharged from hospital. It evaluates the feasibility of a larger trial and the potential efficacy of SAM in enhancing adherence to medication changes and reducing adverse events.

type.justification: The research involves conducting a pilot randomized controlled trial, an empirical method, to gather real-world evidence regarding the efficacy of the SAM application.
type.quote: We conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial among patients discharged from internal medicine units of an academic health center between June 2019 and March 2020.

name.justification: The paper focuses on using a mobile application to improve medication adherence, placing it within the domain of Health Informatics, particularly involving digital tools for healthcare improvement.
name.quote: We designed and developed Smart About Meds (SAM), a patient-centered mobile application that aims to enhance medication adherence.

name.justification: The study revolves around a mobile health application intended to improve health outcomes, which is a core aspect of the mHealth field.
name.quote: Mobile applications have, by virtue of their versatile nature, the potential to bring several components targeting nonadherence together into one tool.
